## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9
    with:
      runtime_ref: a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@a17a2e2e2d69dd60ce3c8460985e621cb28060f9

      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ===PROMPT=== I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

content.text:
We need a Vite project. Requirements: Stranger Things season 4, Dark Pictures Anthology style — quick time events, decisions, story driven, 3D. Desktop game. We need to build something impressive visually: 3D scene in Three.js with cinematic lighting, characters (stylized low-poly but atmospheric), quick time events (timed button prompts), decision making (dialogue choices with consequences), story branching, multiple endings. Use procedural assets (no external assets needed), possibly audio via WebAudio synthesis (ambient drone, stinger, heartbeat). UI with cinematic letterbox, CRT/VHS overlay, 80s title, chapter cards.

Let me plan the game:

Title: "HAWKINS: THE LAST SIGNAL" or "THE UPSIDE DOWN: 1986". Set in Hawkins, 1986, following Stranger Things S4 vibes (Vecna, curse, Creel House, Upside Down). Original characters to avoid direct copyrighted character use? It's fine to reference vibe, but best create an original story with nods: a group of teens in a small town, a psychic girl, a grandfather clock, a curse, the Upside Down. I'll make it an original story inspired by the season: "THE HOLLOW CLOCK — Hawkins, Indiana, March 1986".

Game structure:
- Interactive movie with 3D scenes rendered via Three.js, cinematic camera moves.
- ~5 chapters:
  1. "The Creel House" — investigate the abandoned house, find clock, QTE dodging.
  2. "The Curse" — a friend is marked, choose who to save / whether to enter the trance.
  3. "The Gate" — travel to the Upside Down, QTE fight with vines, decision to use music or fire.
  4. "Vecna's Lair" — confront the entity, dialogue decisions.
  5. "The Last Signal" — finale choices, multiple endings.
- Core interactions:
  - Story beats: letterboxed dialogue with typewriter, speaker names, cinematic camera shots, click/space to advance.
  - QTE: timed prompts (keys like E, SPACE, A/D mash, arrow sequences, click) with radial timer bar; success/fail affects health/plot flags.
  - Decisions: 2-3 choices with timer (Dark Pictures "keep calm"/choice timer), consequences tracked; relationships/bonds with characters; "traits" displayed.

Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment.   if (!state.finalSuccess) return 'ending_loop';
  if (state.sacrifice) return 'ending_newhollow';
  if (state.wrenBurned || (state.wrenWeak && state.method === 'wren')) return 'ending_longway';
  return 'ending_signal';
}

export function initialFlags() {
  return {
    dana: 0, wren: 0, sam: 0, jonah: 0,

    wrenWeak: false, wrenBurned: false,

  };
}

export function createQte(config, {assist=false}={}) {

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D desktop game: a Stranger Things season 4–inspired, Dark Pictures–style cinematic horror episode with quick time events, timed decisions, exploration, and a story-driven branching narrative.

## Requirements
- 3D game, desktop, playable now; no clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks (viewport max 1280px wide); read only the latest image.
- Build request includes QTE, decision-making, story-driven 3D as core features.

## Decisions
- Original story set in Hawkins, March 1986: “THE HOLLOW CLOCK,” with original characters Ryan, Dana, Wren, Sam, Jonah, and the Hollow Man.
- Stack: Vite + Three.js, procedural environments/textures/characters, synthesized WebAudio score (no external art/audio assets).
- Five chapters: I The House on Maple Street, II The Signal, III The Quarry, IV The Hollow, V 3:07.
- Four endings: The Last Signal, The New Hollow, The Long Way Home, 3:07.
- Story engine: node graph (`chapter`, `line`, `choice`, `qte`, `explore`, `scene`, `branch`, `fx`, `end`); QTE kinds: press, mash, sequence, hold.
- Characters are stylized low-poly with rim lighting and cinematic cameras rather than photoreal faces.
- Planned title screen 3D background uses exterior house shot, with DOM cinematic overlay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` (Vite, Three 0.180, Fontsource Cormorant Garamond/Barlow Condensed), `npm install` done.
- `index.html`: full UI shell (title, chapters, settings, pause, subtitles, choices, QTE, exploration, inspect, chapter card, ending, loading).
- `src/styles.css`: cinematic UI, letterbox, scanlines/grain, title styling, choices, QTE ring, inspection panels, pause, ending.
- `src/story.js`: complete 5-chapter branching script with ~100 nodes, choices, QTEs, explorations, four endings, `resolveEnding`, `initialFlags`, chapter/ending metadata.
- `src/qte.js`: pure QTE state machine + validation/display helpers.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio drone, wind, arp, heartbeat, clock ticks, thunder, impacts, chimes, whispers, gate, crackle, record tone.
- `src/props.js`: procedural textures (wood, wallpaper, siding, shingles, asphalt, carpet, rock, clock face, photo, posters, vinyl, silhouette), house builder, trees, dust/spores/rain, light shafts, glow sprites.
- `src/characters.js`: procedural humans with poses/idle/flashlight; `createHollowMan` antagonist.
- `src/scene-helpers.js`: actor/hotspot/skyDome/flames/rain/dust/clockHands/lightning/flicker helpers.
- `src/engine.js`: renderer, bloom/custom film-grade post chain, camera shots, handheld/shake, lightning/flash, raycast hotspots, scene switching.
- Environments: `src/scenes/exterior.js`, `foyer.js`, `bedroom.js`, `quarry.js`, `hollow.js`, `lair.js`.
- `src/scenes/lair.js` just written; not yet integrated/tested.

### Active
- Need `src/scenes.js` aggregator exporting `buildScene(id)` that imports all six environment builders.
- Need `src/ui.js` and `src/game.js` (story runner, UI, input, save/checkpoint, pause, settings, ending flow) and `src/main.js` boot.
- Need to fix known issues (below) and run build/browser verification with screenshots, then iterate on visuals.

### Blocked
- Build currently fails because `src/main.js` and `src/scenes.js` do not exist yet.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/scenes.js` mapping ids `exterior`, `foyer`, `bedroom`, `quarry`, `hollow`, `lair` to builders.
2. Implement `src/ui.js` (typewriter dialogue, choices with timer, QTE input/render loop, exploration hover/click/inspect, chapter cards, toast, pause/settings/chapters/ending, localStorage).
3. Implement `src/game.js` async story runner applying node `set`, flags, strain, actions (`engine.spec.actions.showSam/levitate/setRecordSpin/burnTether/shatter`), checkpoints, scene transitions, shots, audio mood, engine hooks.
4. Implement `src/main.js`: instantiate engine/UI/audio/game, loading screen, title, settings, `setSharedGlow(glowTexture())`.
5. Fix known bugs: `lightningCycle` now uses `(t,dt,engine)` and is fixed in helper; exterior passes no engine (okay). `makeSwingSet` in hollow has an empty group + absolute-positioned meshes (works but clean up). Hollow ground displacement up to ~1.08 may bury actors; reduce amplitudes and set ground y≈-0.4. Foyer chandelier may block shadow spot; verify. Hotspot for clock added. Dana y raised to 3.62 in foyer.
6. Run `npm run build`; start dev server on port 3002 in tmux; use `playwright-cli` and JPEG screenshots at ≤1280px; verify title, foyer explore, bedroom, quarry, hollow, lair, ending.
7. Add tests: `tests/story.test.mjs` validating every `next`/option/QTE/branch reference exists and `tests/qte.test.mjs` for QTE outcomes. Run `npm test`.
8. Write final README/notes with assumptions and controls.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/story.js`: complete narrative graph; must match scene/shot/hotspot IDs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/engine.js`: scene API, `setScene`, `setShot`, `setExplore`, `markHotspot`, `spec.actions`, `onEngine`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/exterior.js`: title background; has `lightningCycle` fixed call.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/foyer.js`: explore hotspots IDs `creel_photo`, `wall_scratches`, `clock_face`, `candles`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/bedroom.js`: actions `levitate`, `setRecordSpin`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/quarry.js`: action `showSam`; gate shader.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/hollow.js`: explore hotspots `swing_set`, `red_tether`, `clock_door`, `dead_tree`; action `burnTether`, `showSam`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/lair.js`: action `shatter`, `showSam`; Dana suspended.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scene-helpers.js`: helper signature for `lightningCycle(spec, opts)` now uses engine from update.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/qte.js`: pure QTE API (`QteSession`, `normalizeKey`, `displayKey`, `qteKeyHint`, `isQteConfigValid`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: `AudioEngine` with `init`, `setMood`, `thunder`, `clockChime`, `startHeartbeat`, etc.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/characters.js`: `createPerson`, `createHollowMan`, `addActor`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM IDs/classes required by UI code.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: all overlay styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts `dev` port 3002, `build`, `test` (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`).

## Important Context
- Story scene IDs: `exterior`, `foyer`, `bedroom`, `quarry`, `hollow`, `lair`; each builder returns `{group, shots, actors, hotspotData, updaters, defaultShot, actions, update, fog, background, exposure, bloom, tint, ...}`.
- Engine expects `spec.update(t,dt,engine)`, `spec.actors` each with `update(t,dt)`, `spec.onEngine`, and hotspot objects with `userData.hotspotId`; engine also generates ring sprites from `hotspotData`.
- Game must call `engine.spec.actions.showSam(flags.broughtSam)` after entering quarry/hollow/lair; `levitate(true/false)` and `setRecordSpin` around Chapter II music QTE; `burnTether()` after fire choice; `shatter()` on final strike.
- `setSharedGlow(glowTexture())` from `props.js` should be called before first scene load to prevent disposal of cached glow texture.
- Story QTE node fields: `kind`, `key` or `keys`, `window`, `hold`, `target`, `prompt`, `hint`, `success`, `fail`, optional `failSet`; game should increment `flags.fails`/`flags.strain` on failure.
- Explore node fields: `hotspots` array of ids, `required`; scenes define hotspot positions/rings. Foyer requires 3 of 4; hollow requires 3 of 4.
- Chapter nodes include `checkpoint: true`; save `{nodeId, flags, chapter}` to localStorage for Continue.
- Browser environment uses software SwiftShader; keep pixel ratio ≤1.55, shadows 1024, bloom modest.
- Preview server is Vite build output via runtime on port 3002 (`npm run dev` for verification).

Now design UI/game.

Key considerations:
- Engine's click listener always picks hotspot when exploreCallbacks set; UI overlays #explore is full-screen with pointer events. Since #explore has no pointer-events:none when visible, window click still fires. We'll handle. But inspect overlay on top might block clicks but window listener still gets it. Need onClick callback to ignore when inspect open.
- UI must manage pointer position reticle (custom cursor). CSS #explore cursor none. Since #explore overlay exists, pointermove on window fine.
- QTE overlay must capture keyboard, and avoid clicks.

Game structure:
- class Game with engine, ui, audio.
- startNew(), continue, runNode loop.
- Nodes:
  - chapter: show card, set scene, chapter HUD, checkpoint save, next.
  - line: ensure shot/scene, apply node set/flags, show subtitle. Wait for advance (space/click/enter). Typewriter. Signal and sfx.
  - choice: ensure shot/scene; UI show choices timer; wait selection; apply set; audio.choose; next.
  - qte: ensure shot/scene; UI runQTE config assisted; result; apply failSet on fail, increments fails/strain; audio success/fail; next success/fail.
  - explore: ensure scene; UI startExplore with hotspot meta, required; wait completion; mark found; next.
  - scene: ensure scene, set shot, HUD time/objective.
  - branch: evaluate when(flags) => yes/no; next.
  - fx: maybe no nodes in story. still handle.
  - end: display ending after fade; stop.
- `set` property applied generally for lines (set on final nodes), maybe node.set. Also node.damage -> flags.strain+1; node.wrenWeak.
- `signal` update HUD bars.
- `shot` -> engine.setShot.
- sfx -> audio.
- shake/flash.
- node.time -> HUD time.
- objective.
- `voice: 'unknown'` speaker class.

Scene transitions: need fade overlay. Chapter card show then scene loading. A small delay.

Async loop: use `await` with cancellation token when quitting/restarting. Could use generation counter. Need robust if user quits during waits. UI wait functions should resolve with null on cancel. We can implement `this.token` increment; each await then check.

Title screen:
- Build exterior scene on boot, shot 'title'. Title screen visible initially with fade clear. Title buttons.
- Begin: hide title, fade to black, start story chapter1.
- Continue: read save, start at node with saved flags and chapter.
- Chapters: unlocked tracked in localStorage; show list; clicking chapter starts from their chapter with checkpoint flags? "Decisions made before this point are preserved in your current playthrough." We can carry flags from save or initial. Simpler: chapter start with current flags or defaults with broughtSam based on save. Could start chapter with flags from localStorage save flags (or initial). We'll provide.
- Settings toggles persist localStorage.
- Pause on Escape during play. Pause overlays with flags summary. Restart chapter -> reload chapter checkpoint node. Quit -> title, fade, engine scene exterior title.
- Ending: show screen, ending stats, audio ending; buttons again/chapters/title.

Audio must init on user gesture. Begin click calls audio.init then setMood per scene. Also handle initial title audio on first interaction maybe. We'll init on title button hover? Better on first pointerdown anywhere to start title mood.

Save: localStorage key `hollowclock.save.v1` {nodeId, flags, chapter, time}. Checkpoint node at chapter start; also save after each chapter card. Continue button visible if save.

QTE UI rendering:
- qte node config. UI.runQte(config, {assist}) returns Promise<boolean success>.
- Build QteSession. Show #qte. qte-prompt text: prompt, hint. Ring progress (circumference 2π52 ≈ 326.73). For press: timer drains; progress maybe remaining; ring progress represent time left. The SVG ring can use strokeDashoffset. For mash: progress fill. We'll set dashoffset = C*(1-progress) or time. For hold animate.
- Key display: sequence: show active key and maybe sequence keys hint. mash target counter in hint. Use qteKeyHint.
- Keyboard listeners: keydown, keyup. Need press/release. Ignore repeat for mash/press. Press once per keydown; mash count each keydown, but key repeat could cheat; ignore e.repeat.
- Tick via requestAnimationFrame with dt, session.tick(dt). On status !== active resolve after short delay (300ms) showing good/bad. Use setTimeout.
- If paused? QTE pauses with game pause: set UI? Engine paused. QTE loop should pause if game paused. Simpler: pause only allowed when no QTE? We can allow but pause screen on top; QTE rAF still runs in real time causing fail. Better: track paused and skip dt. Also input ignored while paused.
- Choice UI: timer countdown; options; arrow keys/w/s + enter? Mouse click. Timer default chooses defaultIndex. Return index. Show choice timer fill scaleX. Input keyboard 1/2/3, arrow up/down and enter. Game must handle.
- Typewriter dialogue: ui.say({who,text,narrator,voice}) returns promise on advance. Typewriter reveals ~40 chars/s. Click/space first completes text, second advances. Should use event listeners on window with guard. Advance hint appears after complete. Speaker shows "NARRATOR" or who. narrator no speaker? CSS. Could show "RYAN" etc. Use who or empty. For narrator set narrator class and speaker "NARRATION"? Story N creates who '' narrator true. Better speaker hidden/empty; set text.
- In text, maybe parse markdown? no.
- UI should expose `clearDialogue`, `showHUD`, `setChapter`, `setObjective`, `setTime`, `setSignal`, `toast`, `showChapterCard`, `fadeOut`, `fadeIn`, `showTitle`, `hideTitle`, `showPause`, `showEnding`, `showInspect`, `startExplore`.
- Fade: #fade class visible/clear. Use CSS transition. Need wait via setTimeout.

Exploration:
- UI.startExplore({hotspots, required, prompt, objective, scene, onFind?}) returns Promise when required found. Hotspots metadata map for title/text.
- Engine callbacks: onHover(id) -> UI hotspots id show label + reticle hot. onClick(id) -> inspect.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D desktop game: a Stranger Things season 4–inspired, Dark Pictures–style cinematic horror episode with quick time events, timed decisions, exploration, and a story-driven branching narrative.

## Requirements
- 3D game, desktop, playable now; no clarifying questions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for visual checks (viewport max 1280px wide); read only the latest image.
- Build request includes QTE, decision-making, story-driven 3D as core features.

## Decisions
- Original story set in Hawkins, March 1986: “THE HOLLOW CLOCK,” with original characters Ryan, Dana, Wren, Sam, Jonah, and the Hollow Man.
- Stack: Vite + Three.js, procedural environments/textures/characters, synthesized WebAudio score (no external art/audio assets).
- Five chapters: I The House on Maple Street, II The Signal, III The Quarry, IV The Hollow, V 3:07.
- Four endings: The Last Signal, The New Hollow, The Long Way Home, 3:07.
- Story engine: node graph (`chapter`, `line`, `choice`, `qte`, `explore`, `scene`, `branch`, `fx`, `end`); QTE kinds: press, mash, sequence, hold.
- Characters are stylized low-poly with rim lighting and cinematic cameras rather than photoreal faces.
- Scene lighting strategy: greatly raise per-scene hemisphere light intensities (physical Three.js lighting + dark sRGB textures require this) and exposure; keep fog/bloom/grain for horror atmosphere.
- Title background uses exterior house shot with DOM cinematic overlay; title look now approved as strong.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold, `npm install`, build passes (`npm run build`, Vite 7.3.7, 40 modules).
- Full `index.html` UI shell and `src/styles.css` cinematic styling.
- `src/story.js`: complete 5-chapter branching script (~100 nodes), four endings, `resolveEnding`, `initialFlags`, metadata.
- `src/qte.js`: pure QTE state machine and display/validation helpers.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio drone/wind/arp/heartbeat/clock/thunder/impact/gate/sting/record etc.
- `src/props.js`, `src/characters.js`, `src/scene-helpers.js`: procedural textures/props/characters/helpers.
- `src/engine.js`: renderer, composer/bloom/grade, camera shots, handheld/shake, lightning, raycast hotspots, scene switching.
- Six environments in `src/scenes/`: `exterior.js`, `foyer.js`, `bedroom.js`, `quarry.js`, `hollow.js`, `lair.js`.
- `src/scenes.js`: aggregator exporting `buildScene(id)` for all six scenes.
- `src/ui.js`: typewriter subtitles, timed choices (mouse/keyboard, default on timeout), QTE HUD/input/ring, exploration hover/click/inspect with hotspot lore, chapter cards, pause, ending rendering, fades/flash/damage/toast, cancellation.
- `src/game.js`: full story runner, flags/sets/failSet, scene changes, shot continuity, node actions, checkpoints/continue, chapter unlock/select, settings persistence, pause/restart/quit, ending flow, special hooks (`levitate`, `setRecordSpin`, `burnTether`, `shatter`, `showSam`).
- `src/main.js`: boots engine/UI/audio/game, shared glow texture, font imports, loading screen/fade.
- Added `this._qteSession` debug handle in UI and `_qteLastDt`/`_qteNow` instrumentation (harmless; may remove).
- Per-scene lighting values updated: exterior hemi 5.0/exposure 1.18; foyer 14.0/1.28; bedroom 16.0/1.32; quarry 5.5/1.15; hollow 7.0/1.10; lair 11.0/1.22.
- Repositioned foyer Ryan to `[1.45, 0, 2.35]`; bedroom Ryan to `[1.55, 0, 1.35]`; updated bedroom `ryan_close` shot.
- Fixed title menu numbering bug (now 03/04 when Continue exists).
- Browser verification started on port 3002; title, chapter I, foyer explore/inspect, QTE success, chapter II and quarry visually inspected; title/foyer/bedroom now readable, quarry still very dark.

### Active
- Visual tuning and verification of quarry, hollow, and lair brightness/composition.
- Need assess latest quarry screenshot at `screenshots/34-quarry-exp.jpg` after setting exposure to 2.4 (result not yet read).
- Need full story-flow verification (choices, all QTEs, all chapters, all four endings).
- Need tests and final README/notes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Read `screenshots/34-quarry-exp.jpg`; if still too dark, brighten quarry rock materials (e.g. raise material colors toward `0x9aa4a6`) or add stronger directional fill; set final per-scene values.
2. Verify hollow and lair scenes visually (`engine.setScene('hollow'|'lair', {shot:'wide'})` in browser, call `actions.showSam(true)`), adjust lighting/composition.
3. Run through full story with real inputs: all choices, QTE success/fail paths, explore requirements, chapter transitions, pause/restart/continue, and all four endings.
4. Add `tests/story.test.mjs` validating every `next`/option/QTE/branch reference exists and `tests/qte.test.mjs` for QTE outcomes; run `npm test`.
5. Run final `npm run build`; update README with controls, assumptions, and verification notes.
6. Inspect console for only favicon 404 (harmless; optionally add inline favicon), then final screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: story runner, save/continue, pause/ending, scene/action hooks.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: DOM presentation, QTE/choice/explore waiters, hotspot lore, cancellation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/story.js`: authoritative narrative graph/scene/shot/QTE/explore IDs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/engine.js`: scene lifecycle, lights, shots, hotspot picking, post chain.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/quarry.js`: currently too dark; rock materials/cliff lighting need tuning.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/scenes/hollow.js`: next visual verification target; has `burnTether`.
